brief:
- what it says: the inherited parent holds what you show the world up against an impossible ideal, then attacks from both sides: you're not good enough, and anything that looks good is fake anyway. So of course your little one doesn't answer when a new grown-up voice shows up saying "Trust me."
- This is where the section's "fake" comes from: the heading is "When the Adult Voice Feels Fake", and Scott said "I feel fake and it seems crazy". Don't name Scott again.
length: two or three sentences, 40 to 70 words
guide_passage: The inherited parent compares the outward persona with an impossible ideal, then attacks from both sides: you aren’t good enough, and whatever looks good is fake anyway. No wonder the inner child doesn’t immediately answer when a new adult voice appears and says, “Trust me.”
next: Borrowed adulthood helps because the new voice does not have to win an internal election on the first day. It can arrive as an outside relationship, written plan, or concrete protective act and earn credibility through repetition.
